historical_reviews.deepseek: A truncated SEL tail is at most a read baseline and cannot cover the Event Logs UI or any destructive lifecycle.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly changes YES and rejects blanket clearing because it destroys the very records needed to prove search/export/delete behavior.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Delete single, selected and all are three different scope boundaries. A successful UI response is insufficient; each requires immutable before evidence and post-action enumeration, and failure of a narrow delete prohibits advancing to broader deletion.

original_test_intent: Validate the BMC Event Logs user workflow for display, search, filters, pagination, exports and progressively broader record deletion without losing unapproved diagnostic evidence.
original_method: Bind the exact log service and preserve a complete immutable baseline/export; prepare owner-approved identifiable test records; verify display, absent/present search, date/page/unresolved/severity/status filters and single/selected/all export contents; then, only under separate authorization, delete one test record, a bounded selected set and finally all fixture-scope records, reading back IDs/counts and audit effects after every mutation and stopping before broader scope on any discrepancy.
manual_activity: The log owner defines retention, fixture and deletion boundaries and separately approves each destructive step; an operator verifies target/scope and preserves forensic exports while automation exercises and records the workflow.
required_inputs: Event Log versus SEL/audit source mapping
Known safe test records covering required fields/statuses
Complete export method and evidence location
Single/selected/all delete scope and readback behavior
Protected credentials and forensic escalation plan
safety_requirements: Do not blanket-clear diagnostic logs for setup
Never delete production or incident evidence without explicit scope approval
Preserve complete redacted exports and hashes before mutation
Verify exact record IDs and selection before every delete
Authorize single, selected and all deletion separately
Stop after any unexpected scope or failed readback
Do not assume deleted records can be restored
Protect credentials and validate target/TLS identity
agent_execution_scope: Exercise display, search, filter, page and export controls
Perform only individually approved fixture deletions
Read back full remaining record set after each mutation
Preserve final evidence and report without verdict
engineer_actions: Approve fixture, retention and deletion policy
Approve each destructive action and exact IDs
Observe and stop on scope mismatch
Own forensic handling and any irreversible loss

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `sel list | tail -n 100` cannot establish complete baseline or test Web searches, filters, pagination, exports and deletion; truncation hides scope and password-in-command-line handling is unsafe.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the supported BMC Web/Event Log API for the full action matrix, preserve complete exports/hashes, and execute single/selected/all deletion only as separately approved fixture transactions with full readback.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All 14 Event Logs actions and 10/10-minute estimates are retained; unsafe setup clearing is replaced by preservation plus an approved fixture, not silently counted as coverage.

modernized_recommendation.status: FORENSICALLY CONTROLLED EVENT-LOG UI AND DELETION MATRIX
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Maintain a record-ID ledger that captures baseline membership, each query result, every export hash and before/after membership for each authorized delete scope; freeze escalation immediately on mismatch.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds evidence preservation, known fixtures, scope isolation and irreversible-action gates while retaining every UI function.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: IPMI SEL may be a related backing source but cannot substitute for Web-only unresolved/status/filter/export/delete semantics; a partial tail is not a complete baseline.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Delete-all may irreversibly remove forensic data and may affect a broader backing log than the visible filtered page, depending on firmware semantics.

project_override_considerations: The Project must decide whether Delete all is permitted only on an isolated fixture BMC or on a fixture-specific log service and whether recovery/import exists. If complete preservation or approved scope cannot be established, destructive steps remain unexecuted and the engineer decides BLOCKED for execution.
expected_evidence: Verified target/log-source/timezone, retention policy, fixture IDs, approvals and complete baseline export/hash
Display plus absent/present search and date/page/unresolved/severity/status filter inputs, result IDs/counts and captures
Single/selected/all export files, exact contents, counts and hashes
For every approved delete: selected IDs, response, complete before/after membership/count and audit effect
Final Event Log/SEL/audit/host-log state, unrelated-log invariance, irreversible-loss/recovery record and engineer-owned verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The action list consistently targets Event Logs. The blanket pre-clear is unsafe and may undermine fixture availability, but the intended workflow remains executable through baseline preservation and an owner-approved known-record fixture without changing acceptance.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The interface semantics, fixture, retention approval and evidence plan are normal controlled inputs. Destructive execution stops if they are absent, but the review purpose is not indeterminate.

review_improvement: Covers every omitted Web function and turns irreversible deletion into a staged, record-ID-bound process whose evidence survives even when source records do not.
independent_technical_reasoning: Log-management correctness includes both returned data and mutation scope. Search or export must be checked against known record membership, while deletion can only be proven by full before/after IDs, not a success banner. Progressing from one-record deletion to Delete all after any mismatch would amplify an unknown-scope fault, so escalation must be conditional and non-retrying.
